previous_statement: There are universal K_step>=1 and e_step>0 such that, for d+epsilon<=e_step, the preceding v^+ obeys sup_n||v_n^+-v_n||<=K_step d and all amplifications satisfy the multiplicative, unit, and two-sided (1+-d^+) norm bounds with d^+<=K_step(d^2+epsilon); hence v^+ is the extended d^+-inclusion required in node 1.
new_statement: Let mu_star=424(d^2+epsilon), which dominates the multiplicative and unit defects. For each n let M_n=||v_n^+|| and a_n=inf_(||X||=1)||v_n^+(X)||. The target C*-inequality applied to v_n^+(X), multiplicativity, and ||X^dagger X||=||X||^2 give (1-epsilon)M_n^2<=M_n+mu_star, so M_n<=1+4(mu_star+epsilon) when epsilon<=1/4. Also closeness to the extended d-inclusion v gives a_n>=1-d-2d=1-3d>=1/2. Applying the lower bound a_n to X^dagger X and then multiplicativity and the target product inequality gives a_n<=(1+epsilon)a_n^2+mu_star; since a_n>=1/2 this rearranges to 1-a_n<=2mu_star+epsilon. Therefore every amplification has two-sided (1+-d^+) norm bounds for d^+=max{mu_star,4(mu_star+epsilon),2mu_star+epsilon}<=1700(d^2+epsilon). With K_step=1700 and e_step=min{1/16,1/(8*424)}, nodes 1.2--1.4 supply displacement <=2d, dagger preservation, and all homomorphism bounds, so v^+ is an extended d^+-inclusion and proves node 1.
